Create a running voxel horse in godot

Build this as a complete, playable Godot 4.7.2 project in the current directory.
- Use the gl_compatibility renderer, and don't enable thread support (it must run as a web export).
- Set a main scene in project.godot. Add a short README.md with run instructions.
- Keep it self-contained: no downloads, external assets or plugins.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory. Don't export the project; that happens afterwards.
- Check it loads: run `godot --headless --path . --editor --quit` and fix any errors.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

arguments.command:
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Voxel Horse Run

A voxel horse gallops across an endless, procedurally generated meadow. The horse, trees, rocks, flowers, ground and lighting are all built in code. The project has no external assets.

## Run

- **Editor:** open Godot 4.7, import this folder (`project.godot`), then press **F5**.
- **Command line:** `godot --path .`

It uses the `gl_compatibility` renderer, so it can be exported to Web.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| W / ↑, S / ↓ | Speed up / slow down through the gaits (stand, walk, trot, canter, gallop) |
| 1–5 | Choose a gait directly |
| A / ←, D / → | Steer |
| Shift | Sprint |
| Space | Jump |
| C / V | Switch camera (chase, side, front, orbit) |

## Files

- `main.gd`: horse rig and gait animation, movement, chunk streaming, camera and HUD
- `voxel.gd`: small voxel-to-mesh builder that culls hidden faces
- `main.tscn`: main scene
EOF
godot --headless --path . --editor --quit 2>&1 | grep -iE "error|warn"; ls

I built a playable Godot 4.7.2 project with a voxel horse that runs across an endless meadow. `godot --headless --path . --editor --quit` runs with no errors or warnings. I also rendered frames from the chase and side cameras and looked at them: the horse gallops properly and the lighting looks right.

**What's in it**
- **The horse** is built from voxels in code: body, saddle blanket, neck with mane, head with blaze, eyes and ears, swinging tail, and four legs that bend at the knee (two have white socks).
- **Running animation:** the leg pattern changes with speed between walk, trot and gallop. The horse keeps its hooves on the ground, rocks and bobs while galloping, stretches its neck and nods, raises its tail, leans into turns, tucks its legs when it jumps, and kicks up dust.
- **The world** is generated around the horse as it runs and never ends. It has leafy trees, pines, rocks, bushes and flowers, and the horse can't pass through trees or rocks. There's a sky, soft sun shadows and distance fog.
- **Controls:** the horse starts at a canter.
  - W/S or keys 1–5 change the gait.
  - A/D steer.
  - Shift sprints.
  - Space jumps.
  - C/V switches between four camera views (chase, side, front, orbit).
  - An on-screen display shows the gait, speed and distance run.

**Files**
- `main.gd`: horse, animation, movement, world generation, camera and on-screen display
- `voxel.gd`: turns voxels into meshes, leaving out faces that can't be seen
- `main.tscn`: the main scene, set in `project.godot`
- `README.md`: how to run it, plus the controls

It uses the `gl_compatibility` renderer with no thread support, and has no external assets or plugins.

`main.gd` also accepts an optional `-- --cam=N` launch argument that sets the starting camera. I added it to render the test frames; it doesn't affect normal play.
